questions.q: What is a WLM query queue?
options: A pool of queries with its own memory allocation and concurrency limit
A list of failed queries waiting to be retried
A queue of IAM roles waiting for approval
A synonym for a Redshift compute node
questions.explain: WLM routes incoming queries into queues, each with its own share of cluster memory and a cap on concurrent queries.

questions.q: What's the difference between automatic and manual WLM?
options: Automatic WLM lets Redshift manage queue count, memory, and concurrency itself; manual WLM lets you define queues yourself
Automatic WLM only applies to Redshift Serverless
Manual WLM disables concurrency scaling entirely
They are two names for the same feature
questions.explain: With manual WLM you explicitly configure queues (e.g. separate ETL and dashboard queues); automatic WLM handles that configuration for you.

options: Adds transient additional cluster capacity automatically to absorb a burst of read queries
Permanently increases the number of compute nodes in the cluster
Reduces the number of query queues to one
Converts a provisioned cluster into Redshift Serverless
questions.explain: Concurrency scaling adds temporary extra capacity during query bursts and scales back down once the burst passes.

questions.q: What problem does Short Query Acceleration (SQA) solve?
options: A short query getting stuck waiting behind a long-running query that arrived first
A cluster running out of storage space
An IAM role missing S3 permissions
A table having the wrong DISTKEY
questions.explain: SQA predicts a query's runtime and lets predicted-short queries run ahead of longer-running queries already queued, rather than waiting their turn.

questions.q: In the manual WLM example given in this lesson, why does putting ETL and dashboard queries in separate queues help?
options: A long-running ETL job in one queue can't consume the capacity a dashboard query's queue needs
It makes the ETL job run twice as fast
It removes the need for an IAM role on the ETL job
It automatically converts the ETL job into a Spectrum query
questions.explain: Separate queues each get their own memory and concurrency allocation, so a long ETL job doesn't compete with dashboard queries for the same resources.
